newsitem.title: USA: Torricelli offers changes to U.S. budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Torricelli offers changes to U.S. budget amendment.

text.p: New Jersey Democratic Sen. Robert Torricelli, who holds the deciding Senate vote on a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. constitution, Wednesday offered a series of changes to the proposed amendment.

The senator, who has scheduled a news conference for later Wednesday to announce his position on the amendment, did not say whether he would vote for or against the Republican version if his changes were not accepted.
"I believe the ... amendment would be improved and enhanced by these changes. Indeed, I believe these changes are necessary," Torricelli said in a speech on the Senate floor.
Torricelli's amendment calls for creation of a separate capital budget for infrastructure spending and changes to make it easier for Congress to vote for deficit spending in time or recession or war.
"Amending the constitution is unlike any other action taken by the Congress," he said. "These are words that will govern contingencies that we cannot imagine, circumstances that we cannot forsee.

Republican leaders believe they have 66 votes for the amendment, which will be voted on next Tuesday. That is one short of the 67 needed to reach the two-thirds requirement of the full Senate, unless Torricelli votes with them.
